head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Pass the slice result layout to a sliced operand with a free layout

Since slice and dynamic-slice can change the layout, a layout required by a
consumer of the slice no longer reaches the sliced operand. That is intended
for operands with a fixed layout, such as parameters and loop state, but it
adds a transpose after the slice when the operand could have been produced in
the required layout at no cost.

Pass the layout of the slice result on to the sliced operand as a
non-mandatory preference if the operand is a constant, an iota or a broadcast
of an operand of rank at most 1, and is only used by slices. Such an operand
is materialized directly in the assigned layout and does not propagate the
layout any further, so the slice stays layout-preserving.

PR #52538: [XLA:CPU] Register F16 conversion libcalls on PowerPC

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52538

Description:
#ai-generated

📝 Summary of Changes
Register `__truncsfhf2` and `__extendhfsf2` in the XLA:CPU JIT symbol registry
on PowerPC, as was done for s390x in #46823, but backed by XLA's own
`__gnu_f2h_ieee` and `__gnu_h2f_ieee`.

🎯 Justification
LLVM lowers F16 <-> F32 conversions on PowerPC to these libcalls, so every F16
computation on a PowerPC host fails at JIT link time:

    Symbols not found: [ __extendhfsf2, __truncsfhf2 ]

XLA's own routines take and return F16 as uint16_t on PowerPC, as the libcalls
do, so the JIT does not depend on a runtime library providing these symbols.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:
None: the new branch is only compiled on PowerPC hosts, which CI does not have.

🧪 Execution Tests:
FreeBSD 15.1/powerpc64le (POWER9), jaxlib 0.12.0.1 built from source (XLA
d867969800d4) with this change and the PowerPC intrinsic device detection
change, without which no XLA:CPU compilation gets this far on PowerPC:
- Before: F16 conversions, F16 add and F16 expm1 all fail with the error above.
- After: F16 -> F32 for all 65536 bit patterns and F32 -> F16 for random

  NumPy; F16 add and expm1 match NumPy.
BF16 conversions still fail on PowerPC, in LLVM instruction selection
(`Cannot select: i32 = fp_to_bf16`), which needs a fix in the LLVM PowerPC
backend.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:Python] Synchronize transfer pull entries and harden socket state

## Problem

Concurrent pull handling and paused fetch replay in `PullTable` invoked `PjRtBufferEntry::Handle` and `RawBufferEntry::Handle` without synchronization. Concurrent callers raced on buffer moves and `num_consumed_bufs_`, while duplicate or invalid `buffer_ids` corrupted entry completion accounting. Zero byte buffers and malformed control frames could also stall destinations, leak slab slots, or crash socket state handlers.

## Change

Claim per buffer slots atomically under `mu_` in `PjRtBufferEntry`, `RawBufferEntry`, and `StringVectorPullTableEntry`, then run `OnReady`, `Send`, and `SendError` outside `mu_`. Count only newly claimed valid slots toward completion, replay paused fetches directly in `PullTable::AwaitPull`, and skip retaining empty entries. Handle zero byte transfers end to end, enforce `IsLastSemaphore` and `SlicedRawBufferChunkDestination` completion invariants, and reject invalid control frames in `SocketServer` without crashing. Existing valid multi buffer pulls preserve behavior and require no new flags.

## Tests

- `//xla/python/transfer:streaming_ifrt_test`: pins concurrent pull replay, completion accounting, lock scope, zero byte buffers, and destination error paths.
- `//xla/python/transfer:streaming_test`: pins paused fetch replay, multi buffer string entries, and empty entry eviction in `PullTable`.
- `//xla/python/transfer:socket-server_test`: pins invalid control frame rejection and lock free connection poisoning under `SIGPIPE` default handling.
- `//xla/python/transfer:socket_bulk_transport_test`: pins zero byte bulk messages and invalid `bond_id` rejection.

display_title: [IFRT] Migrate Client host-buffer cleanup handles to std::shared_ptr<const void>.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Migrate Client host-buffer cleanup handles to std::shared_ptr<const void>.

`xla::ifrt::Client::MakeArrayFromHostBuffer` and `MakeArraysFromHostBufferShards` previously documented that `on_done_with_host_buffer` and `HostBuffer::on_done` were invoked only when `OK` was returned, while implementations wrapped or executed them mid-call before validation and multi-shard creation completed. In addition, invoking `std::move(fn)()` on `std::function<void()>` left closure-captured host buffers alive until the enclosing `std::function` was destroyed.

Switch `Client::MakeArrayFromHostBuffer` (renaming `on_done_with_host_buffer` to `host_buffer_hold`) and `Client::HostBuffer::on_done` to `std::shared_ptr<const void>` ownership across `Client` implementations so ownership transfers unconditionally to the callee and cleanup runs deterministically on both success and failure once all readers finish accessing `data`. Keep transitional callable shims on `Client::MakeArrayFromHostBuffer` and `Client::HostBuffer::on_done` so callers can migrate incrementally.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022069063

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Let slice and dynamic-slice change layout

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Let slice and dynamic-slice change layout

When a consumer of a slice requires a particular layout, layout assignment
propagated that layout through the slice onto the sliced array. If the sliced
array has a fixed layout this converts the whole array, even though only the
slice is used. With a slice inside a while loop the whole loop-carried array is
converted outside of the loop.

Allow slice and dynamic-slice to produce a result layout that differs from the
layout of the sliced operand in GPU layout assignment. The layout required by
a consumer is then provided by the slice and no longer reaches the sliced
operand. Without such a requirement a slice keeps the layout of its operand.

LayoutNormalization rewrites such a slice into a normalized slice followed by
a transpose, which are fused into a single kernel. IsContiguousSlice reports a
layout-changing slice as not contiguous.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

Constructing an `xla::ifrt::Shape` deferred negative-dimension checks to `Shape::num_elements()` and permitted dimensions whose total element count overflowed `int64_t` or exceeded what bit-size and byte-size calculations could represent. Callers computing `shape.num_elements() * dtype.bit_size()` or `shape.num_elements() * dtype.byte_size()` could silently wrap signed `int64_t` unless every backend and utility repeated its own checked multiplication.

Add `Shape::Create` to validate non-negative dimensions and that every prefix product of dimensions fits within `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (`INT64_MAX / 128`, accommodating elements up to 128 bits), returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` on invalid dimensions, and delegate `Shape`'s constructor (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Shape::FromProto` to `Shape::Create`. Remove `Shape::NumElements()`, drop redundant downstream negative-dimension and byte-size overflow checks, and update IFRT unit tests that constructed `Shape` with negative dimensions.

`ReduceDecomposer` runs after initial layout normalization and can insert a layout-changing `copy` that `GemmFusion` fuses into a `__triton_gemm` computation, while post-fusion `LayoutNormalization` skips fusion bodies. Move region analysis internals into `copy_removal.cc`, simplify `LiveRangeRegions` to a sorted computation map, and replace `Relation` with a three bit ordering mask. [XLA:GPU] Demote BF16-exact F32 dots to BF16 x BF16 dots.

***Problem:*** TF32-eligible `dot(convert<f32>(s8), convert<f32>(bf16))` dots run as F32 x F32 GEMMs whose 4-byte operand tiles double register and shared-memory pressure, causing register spills and low memory bandwidth even though every operand value is exactly representable in BF16.

***Solution:*** Extend `DotOperandConverter` to rewrite F32 x F32 dots whose operands are BF16-exact upcasts or reduce-precisions into BF16 x BF16 dots with the same output type, only when the dot already permits TF32 inputs (no explicit algorithm, operand precision at most HIGH, TF32 enabled), so products and F32 accumulation are unchanged.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Preserve empty outputs_bundle_slice_sizes across serialization.

Serializing compile options or executable metadata with an empty `outputs_bundle_slice_sizes` previously reset the field to `std::nullopt` because proto3 repeated fields cannot distinguish empty from unset, causing `ExecuteBundle` on deserialized 0-output executables to fail.

`std::nullopt` and non-empty `outputs_bundle_slice_sizes` remain backward- and forward-compatible. For compile options, empty `outputs_bundle_slice_sizes` requires `SerDes` version 7 and fails with `FAILED_PRECONDITION` when either peer uses an older version. For `SerializedXlaExecutableMetadata`, which is not gated on `SerDes` version, older binaries loading an executable serialized with empty `outputs_bundle_slice_sizes` ignore `has_outputs_bundle_slice_sizes` and fall back to `std::nullopt`.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Fix error-array shape, replicated-shard, and deleted-array handling.

`PjRtClient::MakeErrorArrays` passed `shard_shape` instead of `array_spec.shape` when constructing `PjRtArray`, causing partitioned error arrays to report the per-shard shape as their global `shape()`. `PjRtArray` and `ifrt_proxy::Array` `FullyReplicatedShard` did not reject non-replicated partitioned arrays, and `ifrt_proxy::Array::MakeErrorArrays` accepted `absl::OkStatus()`. In addition, `PjRtArray::CopySinglePjRtBuffer` drained `pjrt_buffers_[index]` to `nullptr` on cross-device `CopyArrays(..., kDonateInput)`, causing subsequent `PjRtClient` and `PjRtArray` operations on donated arrays to dereference null pointers.

Validate non-null `PjRtBuffer`s in `PjRtArray::Create`, mark donated source buffers deleted via `PjRtBuffer::Delete()` instead of resetting pointers to `nullptr` in `CopySinglePjRtBuffer`, delete unmapped input shards on `RemapArrays(..., kDonateInput)`, and check `IsDeleted()` at `PjRtArray`, `PjRtClient`, and `RemapArrays` entry points.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Scale Triton fusion warps up to 16 and 32 for large tiles.

***Problem:*** `EstimateNumWarps` caps every Triton fusion at 8 warps regardless of register pressure while `EstimateSharedMemoryUsagePerBlock` assumes at most 8 warps for reductions, causing non-dot fusions with large live tiles, multiple wide reductions, or wide parallel branches bypassing a reduction to drop to single-block SM residency or spill registers.

***Solution:*** Scale non-dot Triton fusions to 16 or 32 warps when live tile sizes, byte-width-adjusted reduced elements, or independent wide parallel inputs bypassing a reduction exceed single-block register thresholds, thread the estimated warp count into reduction shared-memory checks, keep dot and epilogue-only reduction fusions capped at 8 warps, and clamp to the target device's threads-per-block limit.

[XLA:GPU] Scale Triton fusion warps up to 16 and 32 for large tiles.

***Problem:*** `EstimateNumWarps` caps every Triton fusion at 8 warps regardless of register pressure while `EstimateSharedMemoryUsagePerBlock` assumes at most 8 warps for reductions, causing non-dot fusions with large live tiles, multiple wide reductions, or wide parallel branches bypassing a reduction to drop to single-block SM residency or spill registers.

***Solution:*** Scale non-dot Triton fusions to 16 or 32 warps when live tile sizes, byte-width-adjusted reduced elements, or independent wide parallel inputs bypassing a reduction exceed single-block register thresholds, thread the estimated warp count into reduction shared-memory checks, keep dot and epilogue-only reduction fusions capped at 8 warps, and clamp to the target device's threads-per-block limit.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:Python] Synchronize transfer pull entries and harden socket state

## Problem

Concurrent pull handling and paused fetch replay in `PullTable` invoked `PjRtBufferEntry::Handle` and `RawBufferEntry::Handle` without synchronization. Concurrent callers raced on buffer moves and `num_consumed_bufs_`, while duplicate or invalid `buffer_ids` corrupted entry completion accounting. Zero byte buffers and malformed control frames could also stall destinations, leak slab slots, or crash socket state handlers.

## Change

Claim per buffer slots atomically under `mu_` in `PjRtBufferEntry`, `RawBufferEntry`, and `StringVectorPullTableEntry`, then run `OnReady`, `Send`, and `SendError` outside `mu_`. Count only newly claimed valid slots toward completion, replay paused fetches directly in `PullTable::AwaitPull`, and skip retaining empty entries. Handle zero byte transfers end to end, enforce `IsLastSemaphore` and `SlicedRawBufferChunkDestination` completion invariants, and reject invalid control frames in `SocketServer` without crashing. Existing valid multi buffer pulls preserve behavior and require no new flags.

## Tests

- `//xla/python/transfer:streaming_ifrt_test`: pins concurrent pull replay, completion accounting, lock scope, zero byte buffers, and destination error paths.
- `//xla/python/transfer:streaming_test`: pins paused fetch replay, multi buffer string entries, and empty entry eviction in `PullTable`.
- `//xla/python/transfer:socket-server_test`: pins invalid control frame rejection and lock free connection poisoning under `SIGPIPE` default handling.
- `//xla/python/transfer:socket_bulk_transport_test`: pins zero byte bulk messages and invalid `bond_id` rejection.
